title: Grafana k6
subtitle: Scripted load testing that turns performance into a pass or fail gate.

tiles.label: JavaScript tests
tiles.says: Scenarios are written in JavaScript and live in Git.
tiles.detail: Tests are reviewed like code and run identically on laptops and CI.

tiles.label: Checks
tiles.says: Checks assert on responses without stopping the test.
tiles.detail: Status, body and timing assertions show correctness under load.

tiles.label: Scenarios
tiles.says: Scenarios define executors and workload models.
tiles.detail: Ramping VUs and constant arrival rates model real traffic shapes.

tiles.label: Virtual users
tiles.says: Virtual users run iterations in parallel.
tiles.detail: A Go engine drives thousands of VUs from small machines, making load tests cheap.

tiles.label: Protocols
tiles.says: k6 speaks HTTP, WebSocket and gRPC.
tiles.detail: One tool covers many service types.

tiles.label: Environments
tiles.says: Options and env vars retarget tests.
tiles.detail: The same script validates staging, canaries and releases.

tiles.label: Built-in metrics
tiles.says: http_req_duration and failures are recorded for every request.
tiles.detail: Trends report p95 and p99 latency, the numbers customers feel.

tiles.label: Thresholds
tiles.says: Thresholds fail the run when limits are broken.
tiles.detail: A p95 target becomes an automatic release gate.

tiles.label: Outputs
tiles.says: Results stream to Prometheus and Grafana.
tiles.detail: Load metrics sit beside server metrics, which exposes the bottleneck.

declarations: Thresholds turn p95 into a gate.
Test the system, not the tool.
Script it once, run it everywhere.
